From Yiddish האַנדלען (handlen, “to trade”), from German handeln. Doublet of handle.

parole.significato: To make small talk or idle chatter.
parole.testo: From Yiddish קיבעצן (kibetsn), cognate to German kiebitzen (“to look on”), from German Kiebitz (“lapwing”), from Middle High German gibiz (“plover”), imitative of its cry. Compare peewit.

parole.significato: A meaningless or unproductive job, which contributes little or no value to society.
parole.testo: From Yiddish לופֿט געשעפֿט (luft gesheft), from German Luftgeschäft, from Luft (“air”) + Geschäft (“business”); with spelling influenced by the orthography of the German term.

parole.significato: Dairy, containing anything derived from milk.
parole.testo: From Yiddish מילכיק (milkhik) with the spelling influenced by German, or else borrowed directly from German milchig (“milky”). Doublet of milky.

parole.significato: An expression of disgust, rejection, or disappointment.
parole.testo: Probably from Yiddish פֿוי (foy), from German pfui, influenced by phoo.
Borrowed from Yiddish שמאַלץ (shmalts) or German Schmalz. Doublet of smalt, smalto, and enamel.
From Yiddish שמוץ (shmuts) or German Schmutz. Doublet of smut.

parole.testo: A nonsense word, popularized by MAD Magazine in 1953. Generally accepted to be a derivation from Yiddish [Term?], from German weben + fetzen.

From Yiddish פֿאַרקאַקטע (farkakte), inflected form of פֿאַרקאַקט (farkakt, “shitty, turned into shit, shat upon”). Compare synonymous German verkackt. The English forms with v- are influenced by the German spelling of the prefix ver-.
